title: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
body:
Dibru-Saikhowa National Park, in eastern Assam, is a biosphere reserve at the meeting of the Brahmaputra, Dibru and Lohit rivers, in Dibrugarh and Tinsukia districts.

Wildlife

The park is famous for its feral horses, the rare white-winged wood duck, Gangetic dolphins, tigers and elephants, in a landscape of grasslands, swamps and river islands.

Visiting

Boat safaris from Tinsukia and Guijan are the usual way to see the park, which is best visited in the dry season from November to April.
